Two conditions attach to a grant rather than to applying: artists who are selected pay a $300 deposit, half of it retained for casita upkeep and half refundable against damage, and a no-work policy bars residents from being employed in Taos during the session. Applications submitted by 18 January 2027 at 11:59 PM Mountain Time are considered for three 2028 sessions — January to April and September to December, each twelve weeks, and June to August, ten weeks — with decisions notified by June 2027. — Deadline: January 18, 2027. Fee: $30. Prize: Residency.

item.title: Parallel Voices 2027 · Photometria International Photography Festival
item.description: Portfolio contest run by the Photometria International Photography Festival in Ioannina, Greece, open for submissions from 1 November to 15 December 2026. Entrants submit one portfolio of fifteen photographs, of which the jury selects eight; the subject is left to the photographer, with the festival asking for a coherent idea or a narrated story rather than a set theme. Nine portfolios are chosen and shown as a group exhibition titled "Parallel Voices" at the 2027 festival, its nineteenth edition, at a venue chosen by the organisers. Photometria covers production: the selected photographs are printed on canvas and installed at an outdoor venue, where the show runs about two months, and the prints are destroyed afterwards rather than returned. There is no cash prize or artist fee; selected photographers may take up discounted accommodation rates at properties the festival recommends, at their own cost. Selection criteria are the relevance of the pictures to the entrant's own topic, their coherence as a whole, and their artistic and aesthetic quality. The jury is the festival's own founders and artistic director. Entry is €20 per portfolio, paid through the festival's own photobookstore; the images go as 1500px JPGs by WeTransfer, SwissTransfer or FromSmash to the festival's portfolio address, together with a PDF carrying a bio, project description and artist statement. Results are announced by 15 February 2027. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: €20. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Darkroom Residencies 2027 · Spike Print Studio
item.description: Three six-week darkroom residencies at Spike Print Studio in Bristol for artists working in alternative photographic processes, running January to June 2027. Spike Print Studio is a charitable organisation and, in its own words, "the largest open-access print studio in the South West", printmaking in Bristol since 1976. This call is open only to artists based in the South West of England: the studio states it is "looking for three South West based artists who want to research, experiment and expand their current practice". Each residency gives up to four days of darkroom access a week (Mondays and Tuesdays guaranteed, Wednesdays and Thursdays bookable), a £200 materials budget, a place in a three-person exhibition at Spike Print Studio in June 2027 - timed to coincide with Spike Island's launch of British Art Show 10 - and a paid artist talk at Spike Island, hosted by Spike Print Studio, at which the three residents will appear in conversation together. Named areas of technical enquiry are cyanotype, gum bichromate, lith printing, phytogram, lumen printing, cliché verre and pinhole camera, and the studio is explicit that the list is not exhaustive. The darkroom holds a Durst M300 and a Durst C65 black-and-white enlarger (both 35mm), a printing frame, focus finder, test strip maker, contrast filters, a 1.2 x 1 m Natgraph metal-halide UV exposure unit, a table-top etching press with blankets and a 60 x 30 cm bed, an A2 lightbox, trays and tongs. Applicants must be able to work confidently and independently in their field, must come with a particular project or research enquiry to pursue over the six weeks, and must be willing to lead a small workshop for Spike Print Studio members. The three residency windows are 18 January to 4 March 2027 (no access in the week of 15 January), 8 March to 22 April 2027 (no access in the week of the 29th) and 26 April to 8 June 2027 (no access on 3 and 31 May), with the exhibition and artists' talk in June 2027, date to be confirmed. Applications opened on Thursday 5 November 2026 and close on Sunday 29 November 2026 at 23:59 GMT; shortlisted applicants are interviewed in the weeks of 30 November and 7 December 2026, and the selected artists are notified in the week of 14 December 2026. The application is a Google Form, and it asks for more than the call page lists: a 500-word statement on why you are applying and how the residency will benefit your practice, a 300-word description of your areas of expertise and the alternative photographic techniques you use, your preferred residency window, between three and five images of your work each under 1 MB, a referee's name, email and organisation, and your age. A CV may be attached but is optional, and a Google account is needed to upload the files. There is no application fee. — Deadline: November 29, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Six-week darkroom residency + £200 materials budget + three-person exhibition.

item.title: In Focus: A Juried Photography Exhibition · Art League of New Britain
item.description: Juried photography exhibition in the Art League of New Britain's Low Gallery, New Britain, Connecticut, 5 March - 18 April 2027, with an opening reception on Friday 5 March, 6-8 PM. The League presents it as "the return of a dedicated photography exhibition" to its historic gallery, and describes In Focus as examining "photography as both an artistic medium and a way of seeing" - bringing together work made through film, digital and experimental processes, and exploring the ways photographers use light, composition, perspective and subject matter to shape meaning. The brief is deliberately broad: documentary and portraiture, landscape, abstraction, conceptual work and experimental image-making are all named as welcome, and the organisers say the selected works should reflect "the diversity of contemporary photographic practice and the individual viewpoints that define it". Eligibility is explicit that "works must be photographs" - this is not a mixed-media show with a photography slot. The juror is Florin Ion Firimită, a Romanian-born visual artist, photographer and writer who was introduced to photography as a child through his father's darkroom and later fled communist Romania; his work has appeared in more than 400 exhibitions across four continents, including Paris, Milan, Venice and New York, is held in collections including the Rodin Museum in Paris, and his photographic series The Library has had international recognition. Jurying is hybrid and anonymous: work is selected online from unsigned photographs, then prize winners are chosen in person after drop-off, so the physical print decides the awards. Awards total $400 - $200 first prize, $100 second, $50 third, plus a $25 Honorable Mention and a $25 Juror's Pick. Each artist may enter up to five works, completed in the past three years, original and not previously exhibited in any ALNB show; framed work may not exceed 42 inches in width or height. Entry is $25 for a first work and $15 for each subsequent work, or $15 and $10 for ALNB members, and fees are non-refundable. Registration runs 5 November 2026 to 21 January 2027, with the submission deadline at 11:59 PM on 21 January and notifications on Saturday 30 January 2027. 2D work must arrive ready to hang with wire, D-rings or screw eyes - no sawtooth hangers and no easel-back frames, with prints on metal with a keyhole hanger the exception - and image files must be JPEGs under 4 MB in sRGB, ideally at least 1920 pixels on the longest side. AI-generated imagery is not acceptable; AI-assisted work must be clearly disclosed at submission and must include meaningful creative input, editing or direction by the artist, and failure to disclose may mean disqualification from awards or prizes. Open to all artists aged 18 and over. — Deadline: January 21, 2027. Fee: $25 first entry, $15 after (members $15/$10). Prize: $400 total: $200 / $100 / $50 + $25 Honorable Mention + $25 Juror's Pick + exhibition.

item.title: SAGE Magazine 2027 Print Edition — Marginalia (in nature)
item.description: SAGE Magazine is a student-run environmental publication of the Yale School of the Environment in New Haven, Connecticut, in print since 2006. What began as a small internal publication for environmental graduate students has become, in the magazine's own words, a sought-after publication for poets, writers, visual artists, comic book creators, graphic designers and environmentalists expressing themselves through art; its stated goal is expanding environmentalism through provocative conversation and the arts. The digital magazine publishes year-round and an Annual Print Issue appears each spring, alongside events, speakers and workshops on environmental writing, journalism and the arts. Submissions are now open for the 2027 print edition on the theme Marginalia (in nature). Marginalia as traditionally defined refers to notes, comments or artwork written or drawn in the margins of a book or manuscript, and in these margins, the editors write, "we emphasize, interpret, argue, daydream"; the issue asks what is written, argued, archived and dreamed in the margins of environments, landscapes and ecosystems big and small, inviting photographers and artists to "take us to these edges and peripheries". SAGE seeks provocative, critical, beautiful, captivating work from emerging and established environmental writers and artists, welcomes pieces ranging from playful to pensive, and describes its throughline as strengthening and exploring the relationship between humanity and the environment. Four categories are accepted: prose (personal essays, narrative journalism and short stories up to 3,000 words), poetry, photography and photo essays, and visual art. Contributors may submit up to three pieces. Work must be previously unpublished; simultaneous submissions are welcome, but a submission must be withdrawn if it is accepted elsewhere. Rolling gallery submissions are no longer accepted. There is no entry fee, and submission is through the magazine's own Google Form. The deadline is 14 December 2026. The editors note that response times vary because the publication is student-run, and ask that contributors not email about the status of a submission. The current masthead is Editor-in-Chief Sara Sherburne and Managing Editor Olivia Bayne. The submission form carries three requirements the call page does not: each piece needs its own form submission, only one file may be uploaded per form (PDF, document, drawing or image, maximum 10 MB), and visual work should be a .png, .raw or high-quality .jpeg of at least 300 dpi. The form's Type of Submission list offers only visual art, poetry and prose, so a photograph is entered as visual art, and its required affiliation question reads "university or independent", so no Yale connection is needed. Contributors receive no confirmation email. One thing to read past: the same page also advertises a compensated designer position for the 2027 print edition with a 13 November 2026 deadline, applied for through Yale Student Employment - that is a job posting, not part of this call for work. — Deadline: December 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Trois Points Mag Vol 16 — The Future
item.description: Trois Points Mag is an independent contemporary photography magazine made by an international team of artists based in Paris. It was founded in 2016 as an online-only publication, paused through the covid years and came back in December 2022 both online and as a high-quality printed issue; its stated concept is to promote new contemporary photography, analog and digital, from photographers anywhere in the world, always around a proposed theme. Vol 16, the Winter 2026 paper issue, is themed The Future, and the magazine's question is "What does the future look like before it happens?" The editors are interested in visions of what is yet to come - imagined, anticipated, feared, desired or remembered - and say the future may be technological or primitive, intimate or collective, utopian or dystopian, real or impossible, emerging through landscapes, bodies, architecture, objects, rituals, altered realities or everyday moments: "There is no single future. Show us yours." Submissions go by email with the subject line "Vol 16 / The Future": up to 15 images per project, each file titled with the photographer's full name, at 300 dpi in a large file format and under 50 MB in total. A short text of three or four sentences about the theme is mandatory and is what gets printed alongside the work if selected - the magazine explicitly does not want a general artist statement - together with a brief four-or-five-sentence bio rather than a CV, website and social links, and the photographer's current city and country. The camera used must be named, and captures made with an iPhone or other smartphone are not accepted. There is no entry fee; the magazine suggests a voluntary 5 euro donation to help sustain the project. The deadline is 30 November 2026. CAUTION: the magazine's own website has not been updated for this issue — www.troispointsmag.com/submissions still presents Vol 11 (Autumn 2025, "The Consuming World") as its newest call, with a 12-image cap, so the brief above is the one the magazine published on its own Instagram on 5 October 2026 and the website's guidelines page does not match it. The magazine's standing terms add that every image must be the artist's own original work, that files are accepted in digital format only, that there is no payment for publication — a contributor buys a copy of the magazine only if they want one — and that submitting grants permission to publish the image together with the photographer's name and city of residence. SECOND CAUTION, MEASURED 10 NOVEMBER 2026 AND THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE PASS TO FAIL: that Instagram post no longer serves its caption, so none of the terms above can be re-confirmed at source. The post page still loads with its like count and its 5 October 2026 date, but the caption element renders empty and Instagram’s own embed endpoint for the same post answers “The link to this photo or video may be broken, or the post may have been removed”. Captions on the magazine’s other posts do still read and the account is active — it posted on 9 November — so nothing says the call has closed; but the deadline, the voluntary donation and the fifteen-image cap all rest on one reading of a caption that is now unreadable. Confirm with the magazine before sending work. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free (voluntary €5 donation). Prize: Publication.

item.title: Paper Route: Contemporary Works on Paper · Arts Benicia
item.description: Arts Benicia, the nonprofit visual arts centre that has run exhibitions and classes in Benicia, California for more than 39 years, is jurying Paper Route: Contemporary Works on Paper for its gallery in the Commanding Officer's Quarters. The call treats paper not as a support but as a collaborator: the organiser's own text describes work "from the fluid immediacy of watercolor and the stark precision of ink, to the layered textures of mixed media and printmaking", unified by a single material constraint that "reveal[s] how the unique tooth, fiber, and weight of the paper substrate dictate the behavior of different mediums". All 2D and 3D media are accepted, work may be of any subject or abstract, and photographers are specifically provided for: the entry terms bar giclée prints "except for photos", so an inkjet photographic print is eligible where an inkjet reproduction of a painting is not. Two-dimensional work may not exceed 36 inches wide or 72 inches high including the frame, 3D work is capped at a 36 by 36 inch footprint, hanging work is limited to 35 pounds, wall works must be wired and sawtooth hangers are not accepted. Work previously shown at Arts Benicia is not eligible. One application covers up to six artworks. Entry is $45 for the first work, or $35 for current Arts Benicia members, plus $5 for each additional work up to six - five works cost a non-member $65. The member rate is checked: "Only use the member entry price if you are a current member, otherwise your entry will not be juried." National and international artists are invited to apply. Entries close 12 January 2027 at 11:59pm Pacific, jurying runs 14-24 January and artists are notified on 27 January 2027. The juror is Margot Yale, assistant curator of prints and drawings at the Achenbach Foundation for Graphic Arts, who joined the Achenbach from the Metropolitan Museum of Art, where she was an Andrew W. Mellon Fellow in Modern and Contemporary Art. Hand delivery and shipped work are both due by 11 March 2027, with an artists' preview on Thursday 1 April, 6-7pm and a public opening reception on Saturday 3 April, 4-6pm; the exhibition runs 3 April to 16 May 2027 and work is picked up on 18 May. Work must be available for sale and Arts Benicia retains 40% of any sale, paying the artist 60% within 30 days of closing. Artists who ship must include a prepaid return label. There is no cash award: selection into the gallery exhibition is the outcome. — Deadline: January 12, 2027. Fee: $45 ($35 members) + $5/additional entry. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 17th Annual Intercollegiate Student Art Competition · Center for Contemporary Arts
item.description: The Center for Contemporary Arts in downtown Abilene, Texas runs its Intercollegiate Student Art Competition for a seventeenth year, and photography is one of its four judged categories alongside non-digital 2D, digitally created 2D and 3D work. Entry is free and open to students enrolled at Abilene-area and regional colleges and universities; each student may submit up to two pieces in any medium that meets the category's size and weight limits, and work must be original and not previously exhibited at the CCA. Entries are juried by professional contemporary artists, and selected work hangs in Gallery 3 at the CCA from 4 December 2026 to 23 January 2027, with a closing reception and awards on 23 January, 5-7pm. Cash prizes are $300 for Best in Show and $100 for First Place in each of the four categories, including First Place Photography; those five winners also receive a one-year CCA Student Artist Membership, with the usual 20-hour volunteer requirement and application fee waived for a year. Photographs and digital prints must be matted and at least 8 by 10 inches, framed unless canvas-wrapped or mounted on board with proper hanging equipment, no wider than 48 inches, no taller than 60 inches and under 30 pounds. Submission is through the organiser's online entry form, one form per piece, and work must be delivered in person to 220 Cypress Street in Abilene on 28 November, 11am-5pm, or by noon on Monday 30 November; late entries are not accepted even when the form arrived on time. Unselected work is collected after notification, exhibited work from 25 to 30 January 2027, and the prospectus warns that anything left more than 30 days past those dates becomes CCA property. Awards are Best in Show and Best in Category, with optional second, third and honourable mentions. — Deadline: November 28, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $300 Best in Show + $100 First Place Photography + exhibition.

item.title: Artsin Square Prize 2026
item.description: First edition of the Artsin Square Prize, an international open call run by Artsin Square, the independent artist-run publisher behind the magazine, artist books and the 5×7 photobook series. One artist receives a $1,000 cash prize, a feature in the print edition of Artsin Square magazine, an interview published on the Artsin Square website and a permanent artist feature there, plus promotion through the newsletter and social channels; up to three shortlisted artists get a dedicated online presentation and social promotion, and the organiser states that no further fee is asked of the winner or the shortlisted artists. There is no set theme, so applicants submit work that best represents their current practice, and any visual medium is eligible — photography is named alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, printmaking, textile, installation, collage, digital art and mixed media. Artists at all career stages may apply, collectives count as one applicant, and galleries or arts organisations may submit on an artist's behalf with permission. Submit 3 to 10 works as JPEGs no larger than 5 MB, uploaded through the application form; an artist biography of up to 250 words is optional. The entry form sells three fixed bundles — 3 images at $30, 5 at $35 and 10 at $40 — and its upload field asks applicants to choose 3, 5 or 10 images and upload the same number, so the stated 3-to-10 range is bought in those three steps. Applications are reviewed by the Artsin Square selection committee on artistic and conceptual strength, originality, quality and consistency of the work and the development of the artist's practice, with the committee's decision final. Finalists and the winner are announced in the first week of December 2026 and all applicants are told the result by email. Entry grants Artsin Square permission to use the submitted images in connection with the prize — in the print magazine, on the website, in interviews and through the newsletter and social media — if the artist is selected as winner or shortlisted. — Deadline: November 25, 2026. Fee: $30 for 3 images, $35 for 5, $40 for 10. Prize: $1,000 cash + publication in Artsin Square magazine.

item.title: The Art of Street Photography · TCG Gallery
item.description: TCG Gallery invites photographers and lens-based artists worldwide to submit work for The Art of Street Photography, an online exhibition of photographs made in public life. The gallery's framing is that the street offers no arrangement and no second take — a gesture, a collision of shapes, a person passing through a patch of light — and that what matters is what the photographer sees in the moment. Photographs from cities, small towns, neighbourhoods, transit spaces and other places where public life unfolds are welcome, and the prospectus states explicitly that people need not appear in every frame. Digital, film, alternative-process and mixed-media photographic work is accepted. Work is reviewed for visual strength, originality, photographic execution, relevance to the theme and contribution to a coherent exhibition. Images generated by, or substantially altered with, generative AI are not eligible. Each entry takes up to three photographs — one is enough, the other two slots are optional — as JPG or JPEG files at least 1,200 pixels on the longest side, unwatermarked and unsigned, with a descriptive filename; multiple entries are permitted and the $15 fee is charged per entry, with fee waivers available through the gallery's waiver application. Entrants supply name, email and location plus title, year, medium, physical print dimensions and price or NFS for each work; website, Instagram, biography and image descriptions are optional. Selected photographs appear in a curated online exhibition running 1–31 January 2027 with artist and artwork information, remain in the gallery's long-term exhibition archive, and may be promoted by email and through the gallery's social channels. Work may be offered for sale or marked not for sale, and TCG Gallery retains a 30% commission on anything sold through it. Copyright remains with the artist; selected artists grant nonexclusive permission for credited exhibition, archiving and related gallery promotion. The cutoff has a time: the call is headed "DEADLINE DECEMBER 20, 2026, 11:59 PM ET" and repeats "Submission deadline: December 20, 2026, 11:59 PM ET", with artist notifications on 27 December 2026. — Deadline: December 20, 2026. Fee: $15 per entry (up to 3 images); fee waivers available. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: The Beauty in Decay · TCG Gallery
item.description: TCG Gallery invites photographers and lens-based artists worldwide to submit work for The Beauty in Decay, an online exhibition about what remains visible as things change, weather and fall apart. The gallery's framing is concrete: peeling paint, a neglected room, a familiar object worn down by use — deterioration can expose details that were never part of the original design. It welcomes photographs that find history, tension or unexpected beauty in weathered objects, surfaces, places and the natural world. Digital, film, alternative-process and mixed-media photographic work is accepted. Work is reviewed for visual strength, originality, photographic execution, relevance to the theme and contribution to a coherent exhibition. Images generated by, or substantially altered with, generative AI are not eligible. Each entry takes up to three photographs — one is enough, the other two slots are optional — as JPG or JPEG files at least 1,200 pixels on the longest side, unwatermarked and unsigned, with a descriptive filename; multiple entries are permitted and the $15 fee is charged per entry, with fee waivers available. Entrants supply name, email and location plus title, year, medium, physical print dimensions and price or NFS for each work; website, Instagram, biography and image descriptions are optional. Selected photographs appear in a curated online exhibition with artist and artwork information, remain in the gallery's long-term exhibition archive, and may be promoted by email and through the gallery's social channels; the prospectus gives notification on 27 January 2027 but publishes no exhibition run dates for this call. Work may be offered for sale or marked not for sale, and TCG Gallery retains a 30% commission on anything sold through it. Copyright remains with the artist; selected artists grant nonexclusive permission for credited exhibition, archiving and related gallery promotion. The cutoff has a time: the call is headed "DEADLINE JANUARY 20, 2027, 11:59 PM ET" and repeats "Submission deadline: January 20, 2027, 11:59 PM ET", with artist notifications on 27 January 2027. — Deadline: January 20, 2027. Fee: $15 per entry (up to 3 images); fee waivers available. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: The Narrative: Stories in a Single Frame · TCG Gallery
item.description: TCG Gallery invites photographers and lens-based artists worldwide to submit work for The Narrative: Stories in a Single Frame, an online exhibition of photographs that suggest a story without explaining every part of it. The gallery's framing is that a photograph can put us in the middle of an event, show its aftermath, or leave us wondering what happens next; it welcomes both photographs found in the world and scenes made deliberately for the camera, and says the story may be intimate, strange, humorous, unsettling or open to interpretation. Digital, film, alternative-process and mixed-media photographic work is accepted. Work is reviewed for visual strength, originality, photographic execution, relevance to the theme and contribution to a coherent exhibition. Images generated by, or substantially altered with, generative AI are not eligible. Each entry takes up to three photographs — one is enough, the other two slots are optional — as JPG or JPEG files at least 1,200 pixels on the longest side, unwatermarked and unsigned, with a descriptive filename; multiple entries are permitted and the $15 fee is charged per entry, with fee waivers available. Entrants supply name, email and location plus title, year, medium, physical print dimensions and price or NFS for each work; website, Instagram, biography and image descriptions are optional. Selected photographs appear in a curated online exhibition with artist and artwork information, remain in the gallery's long-term exhibition archive, and may be promoted by email and through the gallery's social channels; the prospectus gives notification on 27 February 2027 but publishes no exhibition run dates for this call. Work may be offered for sale or marked not for sale, and TCG Gallery retains a 30% commission on anything sold through it. Copyright remains with the artist; selected artists grant nonexclusive permission for credited exhibition, archiving and related gallery promotion. The cutoff has a time: the call is headed "DEADLINE FEBRUARY 20, 2027, 11:59 PM ET" and repeats "Submission deadline: February 20, 2027, 11:59 PM ET", with artist notifications on 27 February 2027. — Deadline: February 20, 2027. Fee: $15 per entry (up to 3 images); fee waivers available. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Fabulous Florals & Fine Art 2027 · Pablo Center at the Confluence
item.description: Pablo Center at the Confluence, the regional arts centre in Eau Claire, Wisconsin, opens its annual Fabulous Florals & Fine Art to artists for the 2027 edition: area florists create stunning arrangements interpreting the submitted works of fine art, a botanical fantasia built around each artist's piece, and the organiser's own line is that the exhibit will last only as long as the flowers. The show runs Thursday 25 - Sunday 28 February 2027 in the James W. Hansen Gallery, and the organiser posts galleries for the 2024, 2025 and 2026 editions on the same page. There is no entry fee. Each artist may submit three pieces of original artwork made in the last five years, and the organiser's Calls to Artists page describes its three year-round galleries as featuring original works of all mediums and styles, from artists throughout the Chippewa Valley, the Midwest and beyond - photography is not named as a category and is not excluded. Submissions go by email to the visual arts contact published on the call page and must carry the artist statement or bio, title, size, price, medium and a statement about the artwork; a signed contract must be completed with the received work. Awards are decided by public vote rather than by a juror and no cash figure is published: the organiser's own 2026 results name Best Artwork, Best Floral Design and Best Pairing, with honorable mentions in each. Note three things before you plan around the window: the organiser's own index line reads "Call Open: Dec. 1 - Jan 25" while the body of the same block says to submit now until January 25th 5PM, so the posted open date is later than the posted instruction; artists deliver their own work to the building and are responsible for shipping it both ways; and the house rules state all work must be for sale, with Pablo Center taking 30% commission from members and 40% from non-members on any sale. — Deadline: January 25, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: ABSTRACT · New York Center for Photographic Arts
item.description: NYC4PA's international juried call ABSTRACT asks for photographs that are not instantly identified as that person or that thing. The organiser defines the brief as art that does not attempt to represent external reality but seeks its effect through shapes, colours and textures - sometimes a distortion of everyday items like tables, staircases or windows, sometimes an artistic close-up of a small section of a wall or a piece of art that reads as no recognisable object. It does not matter whether you photograph something abstract or create the abstraction through photographic processes: macro shots, close-ups of graffiti, fanciful post-processing manipulations or simply photographing something at an angle that disguises it all work. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers using any photographic process - print, image transfer, emulsion transfer, encaustic, black and white - with experimental and mixed techniques welcome; only 2-D work is eligible and the jury is blind, so no signatures or watermarks on images and no artist names in titles. Ten cash prizewinners share $4,025 - the organiser's summary line rounds this to $4,000, but the itemised ladder on the same page sums to $4,025: a $1,100 Grand Prize whose image is posted on the NYC4PA home page, three First Prizes of $400, three Second Prizes of $325 and three Third Prizes of $250 - alongside 20 Juror Selections and 20 Honorable Mentions, all included in the NYC4PA online gallery and winners catalog with an award certificate. Two surfaces give different closing dates: the organiser's own call page states February 7, 2027 at Midnight Pacific, while the SmarterEntry portal card reads "Closes Mar 7"; the earlier of the two is published here, so prepare for 7 February. Images awarded an NYC4PA prize within the past two years are not eligible; images submitted and not selected may be resubmitted at any time. — Deadline: February 7, 2027. Fee: $40 (first 3 images); $10 each additional. Prize: $4,025 in cash awards + Catalog.

item.title: 2026 Landscape Award · The Independent Photographer
item.description: The November round of The Independent Photographer's monthly award cycle, and the theme its own Awards Calendar schedules for this month: "LANDSCAPE - November 2026". The brief: "Landscape photography is a timeless art form dedicated to the Earth's stunning majesty. Whether you're drawn to the dramatic beauty of rural vistas or the intricate details of urban panoramas, we're inviting photographers of all levels to share their unique perspectives on our planet's diverse topography", restated on the entry form as "Frame the places that inspire you. From open landscapes to striking urban scenes, we want to see your best work this November." Judge: Isabella Tabacchi, the award-winning Italian landscape photographer and Fujifilm Ambassador whose work the organiser describes as "transforming untouched wilderness into emotional, dreamlike art" and which has been featured in National Geographic; she also leads photography workshops and tours worldwide. Total prize pool $3,000 - 1st prize $1,500, 2nd $500, 3rd $300, and $100 to each of the seven finalists (1,500+500+300+700 = 3,000, which the page also states as "Top three winners receive $2,300 in total prizes, plus $100 for each selected finalist"). Winners and all finalists have their work professionally printed and screened at the platform's annual group exhibition at PCB Gallery in London, with TIP covering printing, installation and display costs, and are featured to an audience the organiser states as +1M on Instagram and +205K on Facebook, advertised together as a combined 1.2M+ following; every entrant also receives a free online portfolio permanently hosted on the platform. Fees are tiered: $15 for 1 image, $30 for 3, $45 for 6, and "there is no limit and you can submit as many times as you like". Judging is anonymous - "a Judge is appointed by The Independent Photographer and the selection process is done anonymously to ensure that each contestant is judged fairly and only based on their work". Photographers retain full copyright. An image that has already taken 1st Prize in another major competition is not eligible, though work that was previously a finalist here may be entered again and can win a cash award. AI-generated images are explicitly not accepted; otherwise any photography-based work qualifies and all post-production editing is allowed provided the result remains photography-based. JPEG or PNG, minimum 1200px on at least one side, maximum 10MB per image. Open worldwide to entrants aged 18 or over. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $15–$45. Prize: $3,000 pool.

item.title: Photo Oxford 2027 Open Programme
item.description: Photo Oxford's Open Programme is the route by which photographers who are not among the festival's invited exhibitors become part of it, and the first thing to know is published only on the application form and on none of the festival's own pages: “the Photo Oxford Open Programme is only open to residents of Oxfordshire.” Read that line before planning anything, because the call page, the opportunities page and the homepage are all silent on it. The festival is produced by Photography Oxford, an active registered charity (Charity Commission no. 1154142) founded in 2013, which has mounted five editions — 2014, 2017, 2020–21, 2023 and 2025 — in Oxford venues including the Weston Library and Modern Art Oxford, with Arts Council support. The sixth runs 15 October to 7 November 2027 under the theme Time, and every Open Programme exhibition is asked to reflect that theme in some way — the festival's own framing is that a photograph is a recording of light at a specific moment, and that it is the moment and duration of the exposure that makes the picture, whether the light is inscribed onto a copper plate or converted into binary code. The arrangement is unusual and the organiser states it plainly: you are responsible for finding and managing your own venue or space, and Photo Oxford says it has neither the capacity to find exhibition space for you nor any budget to contribute towards rental fees — so the real cost is the participation fee plus whatever the venue and the printing cost you. There is no prize and no artist fee. Nothing is charged to apply, and the application form takes no payment, although the page's introduction calls this a “paid submission model” with “entry fees”; what is actually charged comes after selection, a flat £100 for a solo show or £200 for a group show, with 10% off for Friends of the festival, and the organiser says this fee funds the promotional package in full. That package is itemised: a dedicated feature block with an image and text in the printed and digital festival guide, a venue locator on the festival map, individualised artist spotlights across the festival's social channels, professionally printed festival posters, a dedicated exhibition page on the festival website linking to your own portfolio and contact details, and a branding pack of digital assets, logos and signage templates so the venue reads as part of the festival. The draw is the association and the audience — the festival says Photo Oxford 2025 drew over 165,000 visitors, a figure its own evaluation page footnotes as including visitors to public spaces where exhibitions were held rather than direct audience numbers — and Open Programme shows sit in the same guide and website as the invited and international exhibitors. Applications are reviewed rather than waved through: the organiser says all of them undergo a formal review by the festival team together with an independent curatorial advisor, and because it is a rolling process the festival aims to reply within 28 days rather than on a fixed notification date. The form asks for your name, address, website and Instagram, a 200-word biography, a 300-word exhibition title and premise, the venue you propose with the dates or duration you expect, and up to five sample JPEGs no more than 2000px on the longest side. The Open Programme is open to individual photographers and collectives, not to businesses — commercial galleries are told they need a separate agreement. There is no cap on the number of shows, since each depends on the exhibitor finding a venue. Exhibitors may sell work, but admission to the show must be free, and dates may be shorter or longer than the festival itself provided they are agreed in time for the printed brochure and the venue opens as advertised. Exhibitors are encouraged to programme events alongside the show — meet-the-artist sessions, workshops or talks — and those can be listed on the festival website and in the printed guide. The deadline is published as a month rather than a day: all applications must be received before the end of May 2027. — Deadline: May 31, 2027. Fee: Free to apply; £100 solo or £200 group show on acceptance (10% Friends discount). Prize: None listed.

item.title: Artist-in-Residence Program · GENETO ART FOUNDATION
item.description: A Kyoto residency run by the GENETO ART FOUNDATION in ART COTTAGE no.2, a machiya townhouse about a hundred years old near Higashiyama Sanjō whose interior was stripped back to the original beams and rebuilt in white — "architecture as a vessel for artworks", with the ground floor intended as a studio and the upper floor as living space, though the foundation says the use of the building is left to the artist. The current cycle is held with Enryaku-ji on Mount Hiei, the Tendai temple complex that is a UNESCO World Heritage Site: artists make new work while spending time with the temple's Buddhist philosophy and practice, and the finished work is then shown at Enryaku-ji itself for a limited period. The foundation takes about three artists a year for stays of up to 60 days; accommodation is free for the whole period and the studio and facilities come with it, alongside promotional support through the GENETO Group's network and exhibition or event programming shaped around the individual artist. What the artist pays is travel and production costs, both stated plainly as the artist's own, plus a non-refundable ¥5,000 application fee that the foundation says buys the administrative and review process and guarantees nothing. There is no application deadline: applications are read on a rolling basis from anywhere in the world, with the foundation's own framing that it invites artists from overseas to Kyoto, and across all career stages. The residency page sets out the procedure — prepare the documents, pay the fee, then "submit the application documents together with proof of payment" — but publishes no address to send them to: the only mailbox on the cottage site is the one its contact page offers "for questions or inquiries", and the foundation's own directory listing, which asks for an artistic background, a portfolio of recent work and a proposal describing the intended research or project, publishes a general address of its own. Nothing further is charged if you are chosen: that listing states there is no residency participation fee for selected artists and no cash stipend, with travel, materials, meals, insurance and personal costs the artist's. The people printed at the foot of the page are the foundation's officers, not a jury — Enryaku-ji's head of religious education as chairperson, its worship-department director and the deputy director of Enryakuji Kaikan as directors, GENETO GROUP's founder as director, Art Fair Tokyo's CEO as special advisor and LensG's founder as curator and director — and the only thing the page says about choosing artists is that the foundation curates. Photography is one of the disciplines the foundation lists as accepted, and the programme has run before: seven past residents are profiled, among them a photographer working in large-format sheet film and an artist who builds digital collages from her own Kyoto photographs, and the work made in one of those stays was shown at Enryakuji Kaikan on Mount Hiei as "Architecture of Memory". — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: ¥5,000 to apply (accommodation free; travel and production self-funded). Prize: 60-day Kyoto residency + Exhibition.

item.title: CRUSH · Peel Gallery + Photo Lab
item.description: Peel's annual end-of-year group show, celebrating "another year of Peel Gallery", and as in previous years the brief is "peel" themed artwork — "that can be whatever that means to you". The show is titled CRUSH (the banner image on the call page is the only place the title is written; the page's heading is set as artwork rather than text). Peel describes itself as "an art gallery, community event space, digital photography lab, and retail space promoting contemporary art", dedicated to "supporting the work of emerging, mid-career, and under-recognized artists"; its owner and director, Lindsay Metivier, is a photographer, and the building runs a digital photo lab alongside the gallery. Read the terms before you plan around this one: there is NO JURY and no selection — "IF YOU SUBMIT, YOU ARE IN! Don't wait for an confirmation or acceptance email … as long as your work adheres to the guidelines" — and no prize, award or cash is offered. What is offered is a real wall in a real gallery for most of a month: the exhibition runs 9 December 2026 to 3 January 2027, with an opening reception on Friday 11 December, 6–9pm. One artwork per artist, 2-D or 3-D in any medium that is neither toxic nor perishable, nothing larger than 30 by 40 inches, and works on paper and prints must be framed. The practical gate is geography rather than eligibility: work is hand-delivered to 708 W Rosemary Street in Carrboro on 4, 5 or 6 December during open hours, ready to hang, so this suits photographers in or near the North Carolina Triangle. Artists submitting to the show are offered 20% off Peel's own photo lab services if they need prints made, by filing a lab order after the entry form. Entry itself is free and the call sets no age, residency or membership bar. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Madrid Artist Showcase — December 2026 · Arrival Gallery
item.description:
Arrival Gallery runs short group shows in a rotating list of cities, and this call is for its Madrid show, 2 to 5 December 2026, at Calle Valencia 17, 28012 Madrid, Spain. The theme is open and the gallery takes submissions from painters, photographers, sculptors, illustrators, textile, mixed-media and digital artists, describing itself as working with emerging, independent and mid-career practitioners. Photographic, moving-image and screen-based work is explicitly catered for: alongside hung physical work, Arrival presents digital pieces on curated display screens, in digital exhibition formats, in online artist features and in city activations, which makes the digital route realistic for a photographer who does not want to ship and frame prints. AI-assisted work is on the accepted-mediums list.
Submitting work for review is free and there is no entry fee. The cost comes after selection, and Arrival publishes floors rather than a final price: the Digital Showcase route starts from £65 and the Physical Showcase route from £165, with a third 'Featured Artist' route whose price is not published at all. The full format, fee, timeline and preparation details are sent to selected artists before they confirm a place, and physical work has to be delivered or shipped by the artist. Applicants pick their preferred route — digital, physical or featured — when they submit, or ask the gallery to recommend one.
Places are sold from a limited release: when this page was read on 7 November 2026 it listed 40 digital, 40 physical and 5 featured places available, so confirmation secures a slot from the current batch rather than selection alone earning a wall. No juror or selector is named and nothing is awarded — the outcome is the show itself. Applying starts with a mailing-list signup that emails out the real application form. Read it for what it is: a paid-participation showcase, free to enter, where the real decision comes once a price is quoted. CAUTION, MEASURED 9 NOVEMBER 2026 — THE TWO ARRIVAL SURFACES DISAGREE ABOUT BOTH DATES, AND ONLY ON THIS CITY. The call page says “Exhibition Dates 2nd to 5th December, 2026” and “Application Deadline 24th November 2026”; the signup page it sends you to (arrivalgallery.myflodesk.com) is headed “MADRID SHOWCASE — 25TH TO 28TH NOVEMBER 2026, CALLE VALENCIA 17” and states “Deadline to apply: 6th November 2026”, a date already past, under a line describing the venue as “one of Brooklyn’s creative hubs”. The gallery’s five other city forms each match their own call page to the day, so this one reads as an unrevised page rather than a change of plan — but the form is where you hand over your email, so confirm the date with the gallery before counting on 24 November. — Deadline: November 24, 2026. Fee: Free (£65+ digital, £165+ physical if selected). Prize: Exhibition.
